docs.title: Ella IMS
docs.text: Ella IMS lets subscribers of a private 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. It is an IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) that runs as a single application, designed to be easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Voice and video calls over 4G (VoLTE) and 5G (VoNR).
  • SIM-based authentication with your existing HSS (IMS-AKA over Cx), and IPsec between phones and the IMS.
  • Voice QoS from the 4G or 5G core: PCRF over Rx, or PCF over N5 with optional mutual TLS.
  • Application Servers: connect voicemail, conferencing, supplementary services and other services, routed per subscriber by your HSS (iFCs over ISC).
  • Push-to-talk: a built-in MCPTT server for group calls with floor control, and an Android client.
  • Call records: who called whom, when, for how long, and how the call ended.
  • Easy to operate: a single binary with an embedded database, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Ella IMS with Ella Core

An IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) is what lets phones on a 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. The core network gives each phone an IP connection to the IMS. Over that connection, the phone registers and places calls with SIP, and the IMS routes them.

docs.title: Three CSCFs in one process
docs.text:
3GPP splits the IMS's SIP routing into three Call Session Control Functions (CSCFs):

  • P-CSCF: the phone's first contact. It protects the phone's signalling with IPsec, and asks the core network for the QoS that voice and video need.
  • I-CSCF: the entry point of the network. It asks the HSS which S-CSCF serves a user.
  • S-CSCF: the registrar. It authenticates phones against the HSS, routes calls, and involves Application Servers when a subscriber's filter criteria say so.

In most IMS deployments, these are separate nodes. Ella IMS runs all three in one process, with one database, one UI and one API. Each CSCF still has its own SIP port, and the three exchange standard SIP messages, in memory, so from the outside Ella IMS looks like any other IMS.

docs.title: What Ella IMS relies on
docs.text:
Ella IMS stores no subscribers. It relies on two functions of the core network:

  • The HSS holds the subscribers: their identities, the keys to authenticate them, and the filter criteria that bring in Application Servers. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Cx).
  • The policy function has the core set up the dedicated bearers (4G) or QoS flows (5G) that carry voice and video. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Rx), or a PCF over HTTP (N5).

Ella Core provides both. For how it works with an IMS, see Ella Core's IMS Integration.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text: Ella IMS follows 3GPP standards. It should work with any compliant 4G or 5G core, Application Server and phone, beyond those it was validated against.

docs.title: Push-to-Talk
docs.text: Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is the 3GPP standard for group calls with floor control: one member talks at a time, and the others listen. It runs as an Application Server on top of the IMS.

docs.title: A server inside the IMS
docs.text:
Ella IMS includes an MCPTT server, so push-to-talk needs no separate node. It runs in the same process as the CSCFs, which reach it in memory rather than over the network.

Like any Application Server, it learns about its users through the IMS. When an MCPTT user's app registers, the S-CSCF tells the MCPTT server, as the user's MCPTT service profile asks.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: The MCPTT server's name is sip:mcptt.<home domain>, and the home domain comes from the operator's MCC and MNC. Ella IMS routes every request for that host to the server, so the HSS needs no Public Service Identity for it. Changing the MCC or MNC renames the server.

docs.title: Users and groups
docs.text:
The HSS knows subscribers. The MCPTT server knows MCPTT users, identified by an MCPTT ID such as alice, and the groups they belong to. Each MCPTT user maps to the MCPTT identity of their subscriber, sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain>, which is how the server ties a registered phone to a person.

The app reads the MCPTT identity from the ISIM and registers it alongside the phone's own IMS client. Both stay registered only if the phone's IMS client registers with a reg-id.

docs.title: Media
docs.text: Unlike a regular call, a group call's voice goes through Ella IMS: its media relay receives each talker's audio and copies it to every listener. Floor control, deciding who may talk, runs on a separate control channel. That's why the MCPTT server has its own media ports.

docs.title: Authenticating phones
docs.text: Phones authenticate with the keys on their SIM, with IMS-AKA, a variant of the AKA the core network uses at attach. When a phone registers, the S-CSCF fetches an authentication vector from the HSS, challenges the phone, and checks its answer. The phone checks the network in turn, so each side proves itself to the other. No password is configured on the phone or in Ella IMS.

docs.title: Protecting signalling with IPsec
docs.text:
The same authentication produces keys that the phone and the P-CSCF use to set up IPsec between them. From then on, the phone's SIP messages travel in ESP on dedicated ports. This protects the signalling from tampering, and ties every request to the phone that authenticated.

Ella IMS sets up these IPsec associations in the Linux kernel. That's why it needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, and why ESP must reach it through any firewall.

docs.title: The trust domain
docs.text:
SIP nodes tell each other who a request is from, for example with the P-Asserted-Identity header. A node only believes such claims from nodes it trusts: its trust domain.

Phones are never in the trust domain: the P-CSCF takes their identity from their authentication, not from what they claim. The P-CSCF trusts only Ella IMS's own addresses.

The I-CSCF and the S-CSCF also trust the networks in sip.trusted_networks, where other nodes such as Application Servers live. Trust goes by source address, so these networks must be protected by the operator, and must never include the phones. For the same reason, Ella IMS rejects a trusted network that covers every IPv4 or every IPv6 address.

docs.title: Users of the UI and API
docs.text:
Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role: Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. The role decides what the user can see and do, from reading settings to managing other users. See Roles.

The first user, an Admin, is created when Ella IMS is initialized. Admins create the others. Until then, anyone who reaches the UI can initialize Ella IMS, so initialize it as soon as it is installed.

Ella IMS limits login attempts, from each address and for each account, to slow down password guessing.

Programs, such as a monitoring system, use an API token rather than a password. A token belongs to a user and has that user's role, but it cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users. Tokens can expire, and an Admin or the token's user can delete one at any time.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: Ella IMS serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in api.tls (see the configuration file). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

docs.title: SMS over IP
docs.text: Phones on IMS can send and receive SMS as SIP MESSAGEs instead of over the 4G or 5G signalling (NAS). The IP Short Message Gateway (IP-SM-GW) is the Application Server that carries them between the phones and the SMSC.

docs.title: A server inside the IMS
docs.text: Ella IMS includes an IP-SM-GW, which runs in the same process as the CSCFs. Its name is sip:ipsmgw.<home domain>. The HSS's filter criteria decide which subscribers it serves: without them, it receives nothing, and filter criteria naming another server bring in an external IP-SM-GW instead.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text: When a phone registers, the S-CSCF tells the IP-SM-GW, which follows the phone's registration. While the phone advertises SMS over IP, the IP-SM-GW registers itself at the HSS for the subscriber. The HSS then sends the routing requests of the subscriber's incoming SMS to the IP-SM-GW. When the phone no longer advertises it, or deregisters, the IP-SM-GW deregisters too.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text: The phone's SMS reaches the IP-SM-GW through the S-CSCF, and the IP-SM-GW forwards it to the SMSC of the service centre address the phone uses. The SMSC's answer goes back to the phone as a submit report. Without an SMSC, the IP-SM-GW refuses the SMS, and the phone sends it over NAS.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text: The IP-SM-GW delivers an incoming SMS over IMS first, if the phone advertises SMS over IP, then through the MME or SMSF the HSS names.

docs.title: Enable Push-to-Talk
docs.text: This guide enables group calls with floor control with Ella IMS's built-in Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) server. The examples use 10.6.0.5 as Ella IMS's SIP address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella Core: integrated with Ella IMS, as in Integrate with Ella Core, and serving as the HSS.
  • Phones: the Ella MCPTT app, installed as in Install the Android MCPTT App, and a native IMS client that registers with a reg-id.
  • SIMs: with an ISIM you can program.

docs.title: 1. Enable the MCPTT server
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, set the address phones reach the MCPTT media on, and restart Ella IMS:

mcptt:
  media:
    address: 10.6.0.5

docs.title: 2. Configure Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI:

  • Networking → Data Networks → Create: mcx, with an IP pool and IMS on.
  • Profiles → Create: an MC profile, e.g. mcptt. On it, Add Policy: a name, data network mcx, 5QI/QCI 69, ARP 3, May pre-empt, Not pre-emptable.
  • On the MC profile, also add the policies the users had on their previous profile, e.g. internet and ims.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Application Server: click Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT, then Add.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile: name mcptt; under Add from preset, select the MCPTT preset and click Add Criteria, then click Add.
  • Profiles → the MC profile → edit IMS Service Profiles: set MCPTT to mcptt, and MMTel (voice, SMS) to the service profile of the users' previous profile, if any, then Save.
  • Subscribers: put each user on the MC profile, with an MSISDN.

docs.title: 3. Route the MC traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS host, route the mcx IP pool through Ella Core's N6 address, e.g.:

sudo ip route add 10.47.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 4. Add the users
docs.text:
In the Ella IMS UI, go to Push-to-Talk → Users. For each person, click Add User and enter:

  • MCPTT ID: e.g. alice.
  • IMS Identities: the subscriber's MSISDN, e.g. 15550000001.

docs.title: 5. Add a group
docs.text: Go to Push-to-Talk → Groups, click Add Group, and enter a group ID, e.g. fire, and its members.

docs.title: 6. Set up the phones
docs.text:
On each phone:

  • Program the SIM's ISIM with sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain> in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.
  • Set the APN to mcx.
  • In the app's settings, set the user's MCPTT ID as Ella IMS shows it, e.g. alice@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and groups.

docs.title: 7. Make a group call
docs.text: Start a group call from one phone. The other members' phones should ring, and Push-to-Talk → Calls should show the call.

docs.title: Enable SMS over IP
docs.text: This guide lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS with Ella IMS's built-in IP-SM-GW. The examples use 10.3.0.7 as the SMSC's Diameter address and 15550000000 as its service centre address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• HSS: an HSS connected to Ella IMS that supports the Sh-Update of SMSRegistrationInfo and forwards routing requests to the IP-SM-GW over S6c.
  • SMSC: an SMSC with an SGd interface, such as Ella SMSC.
  • MME or SMSF, for delivery over NAS when IMS fails: reachable over SGd.

docs.title: 1. Set the IP-SM-GW number
docs.text: In the Ella IMS UI, go to the Cores page. Under SMS over IP, click the edit icon next to IP-SM-GW Number, enter an E.164 number without +, e.g. 15550000100, and click Update.

docs.title: 2. Add the SMSC
docs.text:
Under Peers, click Add Peer, and enter:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7.
  • Roles: SGd only.
  • Service Centres: 15550000000.
  • Transport: SCTP, for Ella SMSC.
  • Host: the SMSC's Diameter identity, e.g. smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org for Ella SMSC.

Click Add.

docs.title: 3. Let the HSS reach the IP-SM-GW
docs.text: Edit the HSS peer, check Sh and S6c, and click Update. If the HSS's core also serves the MME or SMSF, check SGd too.

docs.title: 4. Add iFCs in the HSS
docs.text:
With Ella Core:

  • Operator → IMS → Add Application Server: name ip-sm-gw, the IP-SM-GW Name of the Cores page as the Server Name, then Add.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile: name sms-over-ip; under Add from preset, select the SMS over IP preset and the ip-sm-gw Application Server, click Add Criteria, then click Add.
  • Profiles → the subscribers' profile → edit IMS Service Profiles: set MMTel (voice, SMS) to sms-over-ip, then Save.

With another HSS, add two iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the IP-SM-GW Name of the Cores page as the server name, e.g. sip:ipsmgw.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and default handling SESSION_CONTINUED:

  • A trigger point on method REGISTER, with the subscriber's MSISDN as the service information, and Include Register Request and Include Register Response set.
  • A trigger point on method MESSAGE, session case ORIGINATING_REGISTERED, and header Content-Type matching application/vnd\.3gpp\.sms.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text: Register a phone with SMS over IP enabled, and send an SMS. ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total should count it, with direction mo and result success.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella IMS snap:

sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control

Configure Ella IMS:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

Start Ella IMS:

sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella IMS repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
cd ims

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella IMS:

go build -o ims -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/ims/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/ims

Configure Ella IMS:

vim ims.yaml

Start Ella IMS:

sudo ./ims --config ims.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella-ims
cd ella-ims

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_ims_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/ims.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5020
      sip:
        addresses: [10.6.0.5]
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.5

services:
  ella-ims:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_ims_config
        target: /ims.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/ims --config /ims.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    volumes:
      - ella-ims-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-ims-data:

Set sip.addresses and diameter.address to addresses of the host.

Start the Ella IMS container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the Multus CNI installed.

Download the Ella IMS manifests:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git

Edit ims/k8s/ims-sip-nad.yaml: set master, the SIP address, and the route to the phones' IP pool through the core's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.

Edit ims/k8s/ims-diameter-nad.yaml: set master and the Diameter address.

Edit ims/k8s/ims-configmap.yaml: set sip.addresses and diameter.address to the same addresses.

Create the namespace:

kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged

Deploy Ella IMS:

kubectl apply -k ims/k8s

Ella IMS's UI and API are on the ella-ims NodePort Service.

Ella IMS's UI and API are at http://<host-ip>:5020. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the configuration reference for all options.

docs.title: Install the Android MCPTT App
docs.text: This guide installs Ella MCPTT, the push-to-talk app for Ella IMS, on Android phones.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Phones: Android 14 or later.
  • SIMs: access rules (ARA-M) that allow the app's signing certificate, SHA-1 692EDA27666062D3982DF420E1FEC26FE806335B.

docs.title: 1. Download the app
docs.text:
Download the app and its checksum, and check them:

curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
sha256sum -c ella-mcptt.apk.sha256

docs.title: 2. Install the app
docs.text:
MDMadbOn the phone

In your MDM, add ella-mcptt.apk as a private or in-house app, and assign it to the phones.

Connect the phone over USB, with USB debugging on, and run:

adb install -r ella-mcptt.apk

In the phone's browser, open https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk, allow the browser to install unknown apps, and install it.

docs.title: 3. Grant the permissions
docs.text:
Open Ella MCPTT and go to Settings → Diagnostics → Permissions. Tap Allow on each item, and allow it in the prompt. It should show The app has everything it needs.

To update the app, install a newer APK the same way. Its settings are kept.

docs.title: Integrate with an Application Server
docs.text: This guide connects an Application Server (AS), such as voicemail or conferencing, to Ella IMS. The examples use 10.80.0.30 as the AS's address and 10.6.0.5 as Ella IMS's SIP address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • HSS: an HSS that provisions initial Filter Criteria (iFCs).

docs.title: 1. Trust the AS
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, add the AS's address to the trusted networks, optionally set how long the AS has to answer, and restart Ella IMS:

sip:
  trusted_networks: [10.80.0.30/32]
scscf:
  as_timeout: 4s

docs.title: 2. Add iFCs in the HSS
docs.text:
In the HSS, add iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the AS's SIP URI as the server name, e.g. sip:10.80.0.30:5060:

  • For third-party registration, add a trigger point on method REGISTER. Set Include Register Request and Include Register Response if the AS needs them.
  • For originating or terminating services, add a trigger point on the session case, plus the method, header or Request-URI to match.
  • Set the default handling to SESSION_CONTINUED to go on without the AS, or to SESSION_TERMINATED to fail the call, or deregister the user on REGISTER.

docs.title: 3. Add the AS's PSIs
docs.text:
If the AS serves its own URIs, such as a conference factory:

  • Add its PSIs to the HSS, distinct or wildcarded, with their iFCs or the AS as their server name.
  • If the server name is a host name, make it resolve to the AS, with a DNS A or SRV record.

docs.title: 4. Configure the AS
docs.text:
On the AS:

  • Trust Ella IMS's SIP address, 10.6.0.5.
  • Send requests to a user to the I-CSCF, port 5070.
  • Send requests on behalf of a user or a PSI to the S-CSCF, port 5080, with orig in the Route header, Route: <sip:10.6.0.5:5080;lr;orig>, and the user in P-Served-User or P-Asserted-Identity.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text: Register a phone. The AS should receive a third-party REGISTER, or the first request that matches its iFCs.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella IMS to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS and the PCRF.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella IMS: installed and started, as in Install.

The examples use these addresses:

Address Role 10.3.0.2 Ella Core's Diameter address 10.6.0.2 Ella Core's N6 address 10.3.0.5 Ella IMS's Diameter address 10.6.0.5 Ella IMS's SIP address 10.46.0.0/16 IP pool of Ella Core's ims data network

docs.title: 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core
docs.text:
In Ella Core's configuration file, set the Diameter address, and restart Ella Core:

interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"

docs.title: 2. Set the Ella IMS addresses
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from, and restart Ella IMS:

sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5

docs.title: 3. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella IMS UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering Plan, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

docs.title: 4. Add Ella Core as the HSS and PCRF
docs.text:
Go to the Cores page:

  • Under Peers, click Add Peer, enter 10.3.0.2, check HSS and PCRF, and click Add.
  • Under HSS, click the edit icon next to HSS Realm, enter epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org, with the MNC padded to 3 digits, e.g. epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.
  • Under Voice QoS, click the edit icon next to Policy Function, select PCRF, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to PCRF Realm, enter the same realm, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Route the phones' traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS host, route the ims data network through Ella Core's N6 address:

sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 6. Point Ella Core to Ella IMS
docs.text: In Ella Core, set Operator → IMS → P-CSCF Addresses to 10.6.0.5, then follow Ella Core's Enable Voice guide.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text: Ella IMS is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella IMS with the --config flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• logging (object, optional): The logging configuration.
    • level (string, optional): The log level: debug, info, warn, or error. Default info.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
  • api (object): The HTTP API and UI.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 5020.
    • tls (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • sip (object): SIP, for every CSCF.
    • addresses (list of strings): The IP addresses the CSCFs listen on and phones reach. At least one; specific addresses, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
    • trusted_networks (list of strings, optional): The networks, in CIDR notation, of the other nodes of the trust domain, such as Application Servers. The S-CSCF accepts requests only from them, the I-CSCF accepts their asserted identities, and Application Servers are sent requests only in them. Must not cover every address of a family. See Security.
  • pcscf (object, optional): The P-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5060.
    • ipsec (object, optional): The IPsec ports.
      • server_port (int, optional): The protected server port. Default 5063.
      • client_ports (list of 2 ints, optional): The protected client ports. Default [5064, 5065].
  • icscf (object, optional): The I-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5070.
  • scscf (object, optional): The S-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5080.
    • as_timeout (duration, optional): How long an Application Server has to respond before the default handling of its iFC applies, e.g. 4s. Under 32s. Default 4s.
  • diameter (object): Diameter, to the HSS and the PCRF.
    • address (string): The IP address of the Diameter connections, advertised to peers. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
    • port (int, optional): The port. Default 3868.
  • n5 (object, optional): N5, to a PCF. Required to select the PCF as the policy function.
    • notify (object): Where the P-CSCF receives the PCF's notifications.
      • address (string): The IP address. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
      • port (int, optional): The TCP port. 0, the default, lets the system choose one. Must differ from the other TCP ports on its address.
    • tls (object, optional): Mutual TLS on N5. Required for a PCF URI with the https scheme. The files are read when the PCF URI is set.
      • ca (string): The path to the PEM file of the CA certificates that the PCF's certificate must chain to.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM file of Ella IMS's certificate, presented as both client and server. Must be valid for n5.notify.address.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM file of the certificate's private key.
  • mcptt (object, optional): The built-in MCPTT server. When absent, the MCPTT server doesn't run and opens no ports.
    • mode (string, optional): ims, the default, or direct: the MCPTT server is the registrar of its clients, without the IMS, for labs and tests.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port on each of sip.addresses. In direct mode, the UDP and TCP port clients send to. Default 5090.
    • media (object): The media relay.
      • address (string): The IP address of the media sockets.
      • advertise (string, optional): The IP address in the SDP, of the same family as address. Required if address is 0.0.0.0 or ::. Default address.
      • min_port (int, optional): The first port of the voice legs. Even. Default 20000.
      • max_port (int, optional): The last port of the voice legs. Default 20999.
      • control_port (int, optional): The port of the floor control channels, outside the voice legs' range. Default 21000.

The SIP ports (pcscf.port, pcscf.ipsec.*, icscf.port, scscf.port, mcptt.port) must all differ, must not be 5100, which the built-in IP-SM-GW takes, and must differ from api.port when the API listens on a SIP address. The IPsec ports cannot be 5060 or 5061. On a SIP address, the MCPTT media ports must not include a SIP port.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• ESP: firewalls between phones and Ella IMS must pass ESP (IP protocol 50).
  • CAP_NET_ADMIN: Ella IMS sets up IPsec in the kernel. Run it as root, connect the snap's network-control interface, or add the capability to its container. On Kubernetes, only the privileged Pod Security Standard allows it.
  • Routes: Ella IMS needs a route to the phones' IP pools through the core network's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requests send a token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is either:

  • an access token, from log in or refresh the access token, valid for 15 minutes;
  • an API token, which starts with ellaims_.

These paths take no token: GET /api/v1/livez, GET /api/v1/readyz, GET /api/v1/status, GET /api/v1/metrics, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml, POST /api/v1/init, and POST /api/v1/auth/login, /refresh and /logout.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role role_id Allows Admin 1 Everything. Read Only 2 Reading the settings, the registrations, the call records and the MCPTT state. Network Manager 3 Read Only, plus changing the settings and re-authenticating registrations.

Only an Admin manages users. Every user reads its own user, changes its own password, and manages its own API tokens.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Ella IMS's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a result:

{
    "result": "Result content"
}

A failed response carries an error:

{
    "error": "Error message"
}

GET /api/v1/livez and GET /api/v1/readyz answer 204 with no body when they succeed. GET /api/v1/metrics returns text in the Prometheus exposition format, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

docs.title: OpenAPI Specification
docs.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella IMS instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 202 - Accepted.
  • 204 - No content.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
  • 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
  • 404 - Not found.
  • 405 - Method not allowed.
  • 409 - Conflict.
  • 429 - Too many requests. Retry-After is the seconds to wait.
  • 500 - Internal server error.
  • 503 - Service unavailable, or not ready. See Check readiness.

docs.text: A call record describes a call the IMS handled, after TS 32.298 §5.1.3.1.

docs.text:
This path returns the list of call records, most recently requested first.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description search query str Substring of the ICID or of an identity of the caller or the callee. start query str Inclusive lower bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. end query str Exclusive upper bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. outcome query str answered, cancelled, busy, rejected, no_answer, unavailable, failed Outcome to include. Repeatable. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id int Record identifier. icid string icid-value of the P-Charging-Vector (§5.1.3.1.19). session_id string Call-ID of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.59). calling_party array P-Asserted-Identity values (§5.1.3.1.24). caller_impi string Private user identity of the caller (§5.1.3.1.36). requested_party string Request-URI from the caller (§5.1.3.1.43). called_party string Request-URI after normalisation by the S-CSCF (§5.1.3.1.9). callee_impi string Private user identity of the answering registration (§5.1.3.1.36). requested_at string Reception time of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.58). delivery_start_at string Time of the final response to the caller (§5.1.3.1.55). delivery_end_at string End time of an answered call (§5.1.3.1.54). sip_status int Final status of the INVITE sent to the caller (§5.1.3.1.57). outcome string answered (2xx), cancelled (487 to a caller CANCEL), busy (486, 600), rejected (603), no_answer (408 after a 180), unavailable (480), or failed (any other final status). ended_by string caller, callee or network. alerted boolean Whether a 180 reached the caller. media array Media types of the accepted m-lines. in_progress boolean Whether the call has not ended. incomplete boolean Whether the record was closed without the end of the call. duration_ms int Duration of an answered call that ended, in milliseconds.

A value the IMS did not observe is absent. Times are RFC 3339.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Peer identifier, a UUIDv7. host string DiameterIdentity of the peer, which must match the Origin-Host of its capabilities exchange. Empty takes the Origin-Host the peer gives. address string IPv4 or IPv6 address of the peer. port int Port of the peer. transport string tcp or sctp. applications array Applications the peer serves: cx for an HSS or an SLF, and sh and s6c for its IP-SM-GW functions; rx for a PCRF or a DRA; sgd for an SMSC, an MME or an SMSF. priority int Requests try the peers serving their application by priority, lowest first, and share them between peers of the same priority. SMSCs of the same service centre are tried by priority. service_centres array Service centre addresses of an SMSC, E.164 numbers without +. Absent if none. status object Connection to the peer. status.state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. down until the IMS has tried the peer. status.since string Time of the last state change (RFC 3339). status.remote_address string Remote address of the connection. status.host string Origin-Host the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange, else the configured host. status.realm string Origin-Realm the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange. status.error string Why the last connection to the peer failed.

docs.title: MCPTT Service Configuration
docs.text: The service configuration of the MCPTT organisation (TS 24.484 §8.4). The /api/v1/mcptt paths answer 404 when the IMS does not run the MCPTT AS.

docs.title: Get the Status of the MCPTT AS
docs.text:
This path returns what the MCPTT AS runs.

Method Path GET /api/v1/mcptt

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mode string ims or direct. name string Server name of the AS in the iFCs of the HSS. participating_psi string Participating PSI. controlling_psi string Controlling PSI. sip array SIP addresses of the AS. Sockets in direct mode only. media_control string Address of the floor control channels.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mode": "ims",
        "name": "sip:mcptt.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "participating_psi": "sip:mcptt-participating@mcptt.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "controlling_psi": "sip:mcptt-controlling@mcptt.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "sip": ["127.0.0.1:5090"],
        "media_control": "127.0.0.1:21000"
    }
}

docs.title: Get the Service Configuration
docs.text:
This path returns the service configuration.

Method Path GET /api/v1/mcptt/service-configuration

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description domain string Domain of the organisation, of its MCPTT IDs and group IDs, and the IOI of its charging. The IMS home domain until set. transmit_time_limit_ms int How long a participant may talk at a time, T2 (TS 24.380 Table 11.1.3-1). Absent if not set, in which case it is 30 s.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "domain": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Service Configuration
docs.text:
This path replaces the service configuration.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/mcptt/service-configuration

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description domain string Yes Domain of the organisation. transmit_time_limit_ms int No At least 1.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "domain": "mcptt.example.com",
    "transmit_time_limit_ms": 30000
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "domain": "mcptt.example.com",
        "transmit_time_limit_ms": 30000
    }
}

docs.title: MCPTT Users
docs.text: An MCPTT user (TS 24.484 §8.3) and the IMS public user identities its clients register at. The /api/v1/mcptt paths answer 404 when the IMS does not run the MCPTT AS.

docs.title: List Users
docs.text:
This path returns the list of users, in the order they were created in.

Method Path GET /api/v1/mcptt/users

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcptt_id string MCPTT ID of the user. alias string Alias of the user (TS 24.484 §8.3.2.7). Empty if none. impus array IMS public user identities of the user, such as sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain>. implicit_affiliations array Group IDs the user's clients are affiliated to when they register.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "mcptt_id": "sip:alice@mcptt.example.com",
                "alias": "Alice",
                "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
                "implicit_affiliations": ["sip:fire@mcptt.example.com"]
            },
            {
                "mcptt_id": "sip:carol@mcptt.example.com",
                "alias": "Carol",
                "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000003@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
                "implicit_affiliations": ["sip:police@mcptt.example.com"]
            },
            {
                "mcptt_id": "sip:bob@mcptt.example.com",
                "alias": "Bob",
                "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000002@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
                "implicit_affiliations": []
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}

docs.title: Get a User
docs.text:
This path returns the details of a specific user.

Method Path GET /api/v1/mcptt/users/{mcptt_id}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description mcptt_id string MCPTT ID of the user, for example sip:alice@mcptt.example.com.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No user has this MCPTT ID.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcptt_id": "sip:alice@mcptt.example.com",
        "alias": "Alice",
        "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
        "implicit_affiliations": ["sip:fire@mcptt.example.com"]
    }
}

docs.title: Create a User
docs.text:
This path creates a user.

Method Path POST /api/v1/mcptt/users

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcptt_id string Yes SIP URI. Unique among users and groups. alias string No Up to 64 characters. impus array Yes At least one. implicit_affiliations array No Group IDs of groups the user is a member of.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The request conflicts with other users or groups, such as an MCPTT ID already in use.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "mcptt_id": "sip:alice@mcptt.example.com",
    "alias": "Alice",
    "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcptt_id": "sip:alice@mcptt.example.com",
        "alias": "Alice",
        "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
        "implicit_affiliations": []
    }
}

docs.title: Update a User
docs.text:
This path replaces a user. The request body is that of Create a User; mcptt_id is optional and, if present, must be that of the path.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/mcptt/users/{mcptt_id}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description mcptt_id string MCPTT ID of the user.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No user has this MCPTT ID. 409 The request conflicts with other users or groups, such as an implicit affiliation to a group the user is not a member of.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "alias": "Carol",
    "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000003@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
    "implicit_affiliations": ["sip:police@mcptt.example.com"]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcptt_id": "sip:carol@mcptt.example.com",
        "alias": "Carol",
        "impus": ["sip:mcptt-15550000003@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
        "implicit_affiliations": ["sip:police@mcptt.example.com"]
    }
}

docs.title: Delete a User
docs.text:
This path deletes a user. The user leaves its groups, and its clients are logged off and leave the group calls they are in.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/mcptt/users/{mcptt_id}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description mcptt_id string MCPTT ID of the user.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No user has this MCPTT ID. 409 A group the user leaves would be invalid without it.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "user deleted"
    }
}

docs.title: Get Metrics
docs.text:
This path returns the metrics of the IMS in the Prometheus exposition format, negotiated from the request's Accept header.

Method Path GET /api/v1/metrics

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
# HELP ellaims_active_calls Calls in progress: attempted and not yet ended.
# TYPE ellaims_active_calls gauge
ellaims_active_calls 0
# HELP ellaims_calls_total Calls that ended, by outcome, as their call records show it.
# TYPE ellaims_calls_total counter
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="answered"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="busy"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="cancelled"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="failed"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="no_answer"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="rejected"} 0
ellaims_calls_total{outcome="unavailable"} 0
# HELP ellaims_database_query_errors_total Database calls that failed, by connection pool. A record not found or in conflict is a result, not a failure.
# TYPE ellaims_database_query_errors_total counter
ellaims_database_query_errors_total{pool="read"} 0
ellaims_database_query_errors_total{pool="write"} 0
# HELP ellaims_database_storage_bytes Size of the database on disk, by file: the main file and its write-ahead log.
# TYPE ellaims_database_storage_bytes gauge
ellaims_database_storage_bytes{file="main"} 4096
ellaims_database_storage_bytes{file="wal"} 646872

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: The operator is the PLMN of the IMS, from which its home domain and Diameter identity derive, and the numbering plan that converts dial strings to E.164 numbers.

docs.title: Get the Operator
docs.text:
This path returns the operator settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcc string Mobile Country Code. mnc string Mobile Network Code. numbering object Conversion of dial strings to E.164 numbers. numbering.country_code string Country code. numbering.national_prefix string National prefix. numbering.international_prefix string International prefix.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Operator
docs.text:
This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC or MNC changes the home domain, and the IMS restarts Diameter and SIP under the new names.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcc string Yes 3 digits. mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. numbering object Yes numbering.country_code string Yes 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0. numbering.national_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. Differs from international_prefix unless empty. numbering.international_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011"
    }
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The policy function is the interface the P-CSCF uses for policy control: none, Rx to a PCRF, or N5 to a PCF.

docs.title: Get the Policy
docs.text:
This path returns the policy function settings and the policy function running.

Method Path GET /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description interface string none, rx or n5. n5 object Present for the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string API root of the PCF, http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. status object Policy function running. Differs from the settings while the IMS applies them. status.interface string none, rx or n5. status.endpoint string rx for Rx; the API root of the PCF for N5. status.notify string Address of the N5 notification listener. status.last object Outcome of the last request to the PCF. N5 only. status.last.at string Time of the request (RFC 3339). status.last.reachable boolean Whether the PCF answered. status.last.result string Result of the request.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "rx",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Policy
docs.text:
This path replaces the policy function settings. Calls and registrations after the change use the new policy function.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description interface string Yes none, rx or n5. n5 requires n5 in the configuration file. n5 object No For the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string Yes http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. https requires n5.tls in the configuration file, http requires none.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "interface": "none"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "none",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Registrations
docs.text: A registration is a private user identity registered with the S-CSCF, with its registered implicit registration sets.

docs.title: List Registrations
docs.text:
This path returns the list of registered private identities.

Method Path GET /api/v1/registrations

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description search query str Substring of a private or public identity. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description impi string Private user identity. implicit_registration_sets array Registered implicit registration sets of the private identity. A set registers and deregisters as one (TS 23.228 §5.2.1a.0). implicit_registration_sets[].hss object Origin-Host (host) and Origin-Realm (realm) of the last Cx answer for the set. Absent while unknown. implicit_registration_sets[].identities array Public user identities of the set. identities[].uri string Public user identity. identities[].display_name string Display name. Absent if none. identities[].barred boolean Whether the identity is barred. identities[].registered_with array Other private identities a request to this public identity reaches (TS 24.229 §5.4.3.3 step 8). implicit_registration_sets[].contacts array Unexpired contacts bound to the set. A contact bound to several sets is listed in each. contacts[].contact string Contact URI. contacts[].instance string Instance ID, an IMEI URN when available (TS 23.003 §13.8). Absent if none. contacts[].reg_id int reg-id of the flow (RFC 5626). Absent if none. contacts[].q number q-value (RFC 3841 §7.2.3). contacts[].media array Media the device registered for: audio, video. contacts[].registered_at string Registration time (RFC 3339). contacts[].expires_at string Expiry time (RFC 3339). contacts[].address string Address and port of the device, as seen by the P-CSCF. Absent if unknown. contacts[].transport string udp or tcp. Absent if unknown. contacts[].protected boolean Whether IPsec protects the signalling of the device. contacts[].signalling_path string State of the IMS signalling path of the device: unmonitored, monitored or lost.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "impi": "001010000000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "implicit_registration_sets": [
                    {
                        "hss": {
                            "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                            "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"
                        },
                        "identities": [
                            {
                                "uri": "sip:001010000000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                                "barred": true,
                                "registered_with": []
                            },
                            {
                                "uri": "tel:+15550000001",
                                "barred": false,
                                "registered_with": []
                            }
                        ],
                        "contacts": [
                            {
                                "contact": "sip:001010000000001@10.45.0.2:5064",
                                "instance": "urn:gsma:imei:35000000-000001-0",
                                "reg_id": 1,
                                "q": 1,
                                "media": ["audio", "video"],
                                "registered_at": "2026-10-26T18:20:04.512Z",
                                "expires_at": "2026-10-26T19:20:04.512Z",
                                "address": "10.45.0.2:5064",
                                "transport": "udp",
                                "protected": true,
                                "signalling_path": "monitored"
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                ]
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Re-authenticate a Registration
docs.text:
This path brings forward the expiry of the bindings of a registered private identity and has its next REGISTER challenged (TS 24.229 §5.4.1.6).

Method Path POST /api/v1/registrations/{impi}/reauthenticate

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description impi string Private user identity.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 202 Re-authentication started. 404 The private identity is not registered. 503 The IMS is restarting to apply its settings.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "impi": "001010000000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"
    }
}

docs.title: Get the Status
docs.text:
This path returns the version of the IMS, and whether it has been initialized. It takes no token.

Method Path GET /api/v1/status

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description version string Version. revision string Git commit of the build. Empty in development builds. initialized boolean Whether the first user exists. Until then, initialize Ella IMS.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v0.0.1",
        "revision": "",
        "initialized": true
    }
}

docs.title: Check Liveness
docs.text:
This path answers while the process serves HTTP. It takes no token.

Method Path GET /api/v1/livez

It answers 204 No Content.

docs.title: Check Readiness
docs.text:
This path returns whether the IMS can serve requests: its database answers, and it is not shutting down. It takes no token.

Method Path GET /api/v1/readyz

It answers 204 No Content when ready, and 503 Service Unavailable otherwise:

{
    "error": "Not ready"
}

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Paths under /api/v1/users/me act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get My User
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Update My Password
docs.text:
This path ends the user's other sessions. It requires an access token.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/me/password

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description current_password string Yes Current password. password string Yes New password, 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 Wrong current password, or invalid new password. 429 More than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account, counting failed logins.

docs.title: List Users
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "email": "admin@example.com",
                "role_id": 1
            },
            {
                "email": "noc@example.com",
                "role_id": 2
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 2
    }
}

docs.title: Create a User
docs.text:
At most 50 users.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address. Stored in lower case. password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes. role_id int Yes 1 to 3. See roles.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 400 Invalid field, or 50 users exist. 409 A user has the email, in any case.

docs.title: Get a User
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Update a User
docs.text:
This path changes the role of a user, and ends its sessions. An Admin cannot change its own role.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description role_id int Yes 1 to 3.

docs.title: Update a User's Password
docs.text:
This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Delete a User
docs.text:
This path deletes the user with its sessions and API tokens. An Admin cannot delete itself.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Create an API Token
docs.text:
This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens POST /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens. expires_at string No RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 400 Invalid field, or 12 tokens exist. 409 The user has a token of that name.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "name": "Monitoring",
    "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellaims_aB3dE5fG7hJ9_KQ4ZN2X7WJ5R3TQY6PLM2VA4CF"
    }
}

docs.title: List API Tokens
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens GET /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Token identifier: the part of the token between ellaims_ and the next _. name string Name. created_at string Creation time. expires_at string Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire. last_used_at string Time of the last use, to the minute. Absent for a token never used.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "aB3dE5fG7hJ9",
                "name": "Monitoring",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-10-27T19:02:00.000Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Delete an API Token
docs.text: Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id} DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add voice calls to a private 5G network with Ella IMS.

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Make Your First Voice Call An Ella Core 5G network, a second Linux host, two phones Snap ~30 min

docs.title: Make Your First Voice Call
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add Ella IMS to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and make a voice call (VoNR) between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

Ella Core

  • A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware) tutorial. In this tutorial, Ella Core's N6 interface, ens3, has the address 10.6.0.2.

Ella IMS

  • A second Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, on Ella Core's N6 network. In this tutorial, it has the address 10.6.0.5.

Phones

  • Two 5G phones that support VoNR, each with a SIM provisioned as a subscriber in Ella Core.

docs.title: 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core
docs.text:
On the Ella Core machine, edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

Under interfaces, add the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.6.0.2"

Restart Ella Core:

sudo snap restart ella-core.cored

docs.title: 2. Install Ella IMS
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, install the Ella IMS snap:

sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control

Edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

Set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from:

/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5

Start Ella IMS:

sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd

docs.title: 3. Initialize Ella IMS
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to http://10.6.0.5:5020/. The Initialize Ella IMS page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click Create. You should see Ella IMS's Cores page.

docs.title: 4. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core
docs.text:
Go to the Cores page:

  • Under Peers, click Add Peer, enter 10.6.0.2, check HSS and PCRF, and click Add.
  • Under HSS, click the edit icon next to HSS Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.
  • Under Voice QoS, click the edit icon next to Policy Function, select PCRF, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to PCRF Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.

Under Peers, Ella Core should show as open.

docs.title: 5. Route the phones' traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, route the phones' voice addresses, which we create in the next step, through Ella Core:

sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 6. Prepare Ella Core for voice
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to the Operator page and scroll to the IMS section. Click the edit icon next to P-CSCF Addresses, enter 10.6.0.5, and click Update.

Go to the Networking page and open the Data Networks tab. Click Create, enter ims as the Name, 10.46.0.0/16 as the IPv4 Pool, turn on IMS (voice and mission critical services), and click Create.

Go to the Profiles page and click on the default profile. Click Add Policy, enter voice as the Name, set the Data Network to ims, and click Create.

Go to the Subscribers page. For each of the two subscribers, click on it, click the edit icon next to MSISDN, enter a number, and click Update:

  • First subscriber: +15551230001
  • Second subscriber: +15551230002

docs.title: 7. Register the phones
docs.text:
On each phone, turn on VoNR, then turn airplane mode on and off.

In Ella IMS, go to the Registrations page. You should see both phones.

docs.title: 8. Make a call
docs.text:
From the first phone, call +15551230002. Answer on the second phone, talk, and hang up.

In Ella IMS, go to the Calls page. You should see the call, with the outcome answered.

Success

Congratulations! You have made a voice call over your private 5G network, through Ella Core and Ella IMS.
